chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from he who mentioned him, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorced woman, does she perform Hajj during her waiting period? He said, 'If she is newly divorced (before consummation), she performs Hajj during her waiting period. And if she has already performed Hajj, she does not perform Hajj until her waiting period is completed.' As for the waiting period of the woman whose husband has died, it is permissible for her to go out during it, and we have previously mentioned that, and what is narrated adds to its clarification:

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: The woman whose husband has died (widow)

ai.seo_question: Can a divorced woman perform Hajj during her waiting period (Iddah)?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Barqi, transmitted through Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, clarifies the distinction between a 'surrah' (divorced before consummation) and a 'mu'abbadah' (divorced after consummation) regarding Hajj eligibility during their respective waiting periods. It highlights the juristic principle that the 'iddah' of a widow is less restrictive than that of a divorcee, allowing for travel and worship earlier, a point further elucidated by the subsequent text referenced by the compiler. This ruling underscores the practical implications of marital status on ritual obligations in Shia fiqh.
